status_reasoning: Reviewers request validation of NMI identification by orthogonal methods (bisulphite sequencing, pyrosequencing, or EpiTyping), stating 'This is mentioned as data not shown but please provide some examples.' While the Bio-CAP methodology is not rejected, the reviewers indicate that additional validation is needed to fully support confidence in the method's ability to identify NMIs.

Reviewers accept the explanation for species differences in sequence composition but request better presentation and citation. They ask authors to 'briefly summarise (perhaps in the Introduction) why the different species have such different sequence composition' and cite prior work (PMID: 17932072). The underlying claims about sequence variation are not challenged, only their presentation and attribution.

Reviewers question the framing that NMIs at promoters are 'contrary to expectations,' stating 'It is not clear why the authors talk about NMIs at promoters being "contrary to expectations", when the opposite is probably more generally accepted.' This suggests the reviewers believe the finding itself may not be as surprising as the authors claim, requesting justification or revision of this characterization.

Reviewers acknowledge a methodological limitation, noting 'an affinity approach (such as the use of the CXXC reagent) is more likely to be sensitive to CpG-dense than CpG-depleted loci,' but explicitly state 'this does not influence the conclusions.' The claims about Bio-CAP's ability to detect NMIs across CpG density ranges are accepted with the caveat that this limitation should be acknowledged.

The reviewers do not challenge the finding that CGI predictions fail to accurately identify NMIs across species. They request acknowledgment that 'the annotation is performed on repeat masked sequence, so the quality of the annotation of repetitive elements also plays a role' (Comment 6), but this is presented as an additional factor to acknowledge rather than a critique of the main finding.

The core findings about NMI conservation across vertebrates, their presence at orthologous genes, and the unprecedented level of epigenetic conservation are not questioned by reviewers. The general assessment states this is 'a well executed, clearly presented original piece of work and publication is recommended,' with no concerns raised about these central claims.

The findings about tissue-specific differential methylation of NMIs and the characterization of 'plastic' NMIs are not challenged by reviewers. No concerns are raised about these observations, and they are implicitly accepted as part of the 'well executed' work.

The identification and characterization of three distinct classes of NMIs, including broad NMIs associated with developmental genes and polycomb regulation, are not questioned by reviewers. These findings are implicitly accepted as part of the overall positive assessment of the manuscript.

The observations about intergenic NMIs and their association with lncRNAs and regulatory elements are not challenged by reviewers. These findings are accepted without comment as part of the overall work.
